jane_street.interpretation: Jane Street's Bitwise share count declined while Canary and Franklin share counts rose. Large listed call/put positions and separate linked/leveraged ETF holdings make simple directional interpretation invalid. The filings do not identify the ultimate beneficial owner or trading motive.

limitations: 13F is quarterly and lagged: Q3 holdings are as of 2026-09-30 and were filed 2026-11-12 or 2026-11-16.
ETF share counts are not XRP token units and reported market values are quarter-end valuations, not actual cash purchases.
13F does not disclose short positions and does not provide option strike/expiry or complete delta-adjusted exposure in these rows.
The filings do not distinguish proprietary holdings from customer, market-making, arbitrage, custody, or hedged inventory.
No direct XRP token balance, on-chain holding, spot exchange purchase, ETF creation/redemption, or daily flow is established.
SEC information tables themselves warn that the Commission has not necessarily reviewed accuracy or completeness.
Raw SEC response bytes were not captured in this run; hashes cover normalized extracted row strings only.
competing_hypotheses: Reported ETF shares may represent institutional investment exposure, customer positions, market-making inventory, arbitrage, or collateral/hedging activity.
Jane Street's issuer-level changes may reflect rotation between ETF issuers or market-making inventory changes rather than net XRP accumulation or distribution.
The leveraged and option positions may be hedges or structured trading exposures; their presence is not a bullish or bearish directional signal.
disconfirming_evidence: Jane Street's Bitwise XRP ETF common share count fell 39.13% from Q2 to Q3.
Jane Street reported large Canary call and put positions, which cannot be netted from the 13F data alone.
Susquehanna reported both Bitwise calls and puts alongside common ETF shares.
No direct XRP token position or on-chain balance is identified by these filings.
